# AMD v3: dated operating valuation and equity-claim update

Information checked through October 18, 2026. Valuation origin: June 27, 2026. USD unless stated.

## Readiness and headline

**Ready for qualified, dated operating research. Show operating EV, not a common-share price.** Missing October balances do not block this deliverable. The unchanged model reconstructs June-origin value using later guidance and commitments; it is not a June information-set backtest. The acquired businesses, new borrowing and its uses of proceeds are not silently mixed into the old valuation bridge.

| Conditional operating case | Operating EV | Selected incremental investment return |
|---|---:|---:|
| Deployment delay | $85.529B | 12% |
| Base | $347.857B | 20% |
| Platform scale | $790.813B | 25% |

These are analyst operating scenarios before customer equity rebates and future partner-asset flows, not probability-weighted fair values or share-price bounds. The base becomes $303.364B at a fully rebuilt 12% incremental return and $321.340B when all new economic investment rises 25%. Capital intensity remains a major valuation judgment. Historical guidance success does not validate that judgment.

The dated residual pools remain $87.948B / $354.366B / $800.024B, respectively. Their precise label is **after selected ESPP reserves, before remaining legacy employee and customer claims**. Those reserves are $150M / $100M / $100M. The pools are appendix arithmetic, not common equity. A measured ESPP claim would replace the reserve. Current common-equity and per-share outputs remain null.

The prior independent v2 review remains valid for its stated operating/conditional scope. This v3 adds material events and internal checks; it does not claim a new independent audit or authorize publication.

## 1. Material post-origin financing now identified

AMD closed $4.750B of senior notes on August 17: $1.250B at 4.600%, $1.500B at 5.000%, $1.000B at 5.250%, and $1.000B at 5.500%, maturing August 17 in 2029, 2031, 2033 and 2036. Annual coupon cash is **$240M**. The first semiannual payments are due February 17, 2027. [Closing 8-K](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-354029/d142696d8k.htm)

The prospectus's June as-adjusted capitalization increases cash from $5.086B to $9.812B, implying **$4.726B estimated net proceeds**, while principal rises $4.750B. The **$24M** difference is the rounded discount/issuance-cost effect under the principal-basis bridge. The prose rounds proceeds to $4.7B. This is not an actual October balance or a subsequently reported exact receipt. [Prospectus, S-17–18](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-352628/d173126d424b5.htm)

The older $875M note matured contractually on September 24. Actual retirement was not established in the reviewed material. If retired, it reduces cash and principal equally; its $36.855M annual coupon disappears. The September semiannual coupon is $18.4275M and covers a period crossing the June origin. [Original note terms](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-061366/d914634d8k.htm)

Financing-only illustration, excluding every other cash flow and assuming proceeds retained and that maturity paid:
- Cash plus short investments: $13.111B + $4.726B − $0.875B = **$16.962B**
- Senior principal: $3.250B + $4.750B − $0.875B = **$7.125B**
- Net cash less senior principal: **$9.837B**, $24M below the opening $9.861B
- Annual coupon increase: **$203.145M**

These are conditional transactions, not current balances. The source also discloses approximately $65,000 of convertible principal rounded to zero in its million-dollar table; the illustration does not assert its subsequent status. Adding debt without proceeds would create a false $4.75B value loss. Adding proceeds without debt would create false value. Coupons belong in financing/liquidity analysis, not as a second subtraction from unlevered FCFF when debt is separately allocated. A current valuation would also require consistent debt market value, financing tax and WACC treatment.

## 2. Acquisition shares and commercial investment are different claims

**World Labs:** The September 26 merger agreement provides approximately $8.2B of AMD shares, subject to adjustments. Shares depend on the ten-day VWAP window ending on the second trading day before closing, so there is no fixed current issuance count. [Transaction 8-K](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0000002488-26-000182/amd-20260926.htm) The announced close is expected by year-end, subject to approvals and conditions. [Issuer announcement](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1299/amd-to-acquire-world-labs-to-advance-the-future-of-ai-compute)

At closing, issued shares = adjusted consideration / contractual VWAP. A combined valuation must add independently valued target economics, acquired assets/liabilities and integration costs once, then allocate ownership. Do not deduct $8.2B cash and also dilute, or equate announced price to acquired intrinsic value. Replacement awards, existing-investment overlap and target cash flows remain unknown. The operating scenarios here exclude an incremental World Labs contribution and its issuance.

**Taalas:** Despite the headline “acquires,” the August 6 release describes a definitive agreement subject to closing conditions and approvals. Consideration and payment mix are not given; completed closing was not established. No acquisition cash debit, shares or target value is invented. [Issuer announcement](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1296/amd-acquires-taalas-to-advance-compute-solutions-for-rapidly-growing-ai-inference-market)

**Anthropic:** The July 22 release identifies up to $5B of strategic equity investment alongside planned deployment of up to 2 GW, starting with 1 GW in H1 2027. [Issuer announcement](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1292/amd-and-anthropic-announce-strategic-partnership-to-deploy-up-to-2-gigawatts-of-amd-instinct-mi450-series-gpus) Match this to the v2 $5B subsequent-investment exposure rather than adding another $5B. The amount/timing match is an analyst reconciliation; the 10-Q does not expressly identify that counterparty. The selected $1B/$2B/$2B funding and 2030 recoveries remain assumptions. No equity ownership, preference, return or liquidity date has been inferred.

## 3. Employee and customer claim treatment

The June filing supplies plan capacity, common-share movements and expense, not a complete outstanding-award valuation. Authorized shares minus available shares is not an outstanding award count. Diluted EPS weighted shares are not a current economic-claim ledger. [June 10-Q, Note 12](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0000002488-26-000123/amd-20260627.htm)

The July executive disclosure adds a specific cohort: five executives' August 15 target awards total **$70.5M**, split $47.7M performance and $22.8M time-based target value. Shares are converted using a 30-trading-day average. Performance payouts span 0–250% of target and generally require service to August 2029; time units vest from August 2027 through August 2030. Target values are not current option fair values or confirmed current share counts. [July 8-K](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0000002488-26-000115/amd-20260626.htm)

Future grant cost already stays in modeled EBIT. A cohort-level bridge must avoid charging future service twice through both operating expense and a full claim deduction. The August grants cannot automatically become an additional $70.5M legacy deduction. Failed Form 4 retrievals are recorded; no company-wide current ledger is claimed.

The v2 OpenAI/Meta public facts and explicit conditional paths remain unchanged: each program permits up to 160M original shares; initial 1 GW commitments are binding; 6 GW full-vesting purchase conditions and $600 final-tranche thresholds coexist with other conditions. Intermediate vesting/exercise schedules remain redacted. Cashless-exercise VWAP definitions must not be confused with vesting-barrier measurement rules. The pathways do not establish actual October barrier status, probability, fair value or customer-specific dollar revenue. No aggregate independent dilution grid is restored. [OpenAI contract](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-230895/d28189dex41.htm), [Meta contract](https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0000002488-26-000045/a41commonstockwarrantagree.htm)

## 4. Funding controls and remaining uncertainty

Ordinary purchase/cloud commitments fund costs or working capital; they are not automatically debt. Direct lease rent already appears in operating costs. Partner guarantees remain contingent loss exposures. Investments create separate assets with uncertain recoveries. None is summed blindly into a gross “debt” claim. Undrawn credit lines are neither cash nor value and should not be added together as guaranteed independent liquidity.

The original funding stresses remain useful: lower returns, zero partner recovery, full initial guarantee loss and loss of related asset recoveries. They are stresses, not probabilities or legal loss limits. Contract-level overlap, cancellation, capacity assignment, guarantee rolloff and supplier prepayments remain unavailable. The loan-interest exclusion is intended but unquantified; only principal and restricted cash were numerically removed from opening prepaids. That classification uncertainty is not a new measured cash-flow adjustment.

## 5. Management guidance credibility

The fixed recent window includes every quarter from Q1 2024 through Q2 2026: **10/10 revenues above midpoint**, **5 above the upper range**, **5 inside**, and none below the lower range. Mean midpoint beat is **3.709%**, median **3.426%**. This is a selected recent cycle, not a statistical probability of future success. Original guidance and actual source URLs accompany every row in the scorecard.

Q4 2025's reported 6.979% revenue beat includes about $390M of China MI308 sales excluded from guidance. Removing only that identified item gives $9.880B versus $9.600B midpoint, a **2.917% beat within the original range**. Reported 57% non-GAAP gross margin benefited from the inventory reserve reversal; AMD's exclusion of both China sales and that reversal gives approximately 55%, versus 54.5% guidance. This is one isolated normalization, not a complete constant-mix measure. [Q4 2025 release](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1276/amd-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results)

The FY2022 counterexample remains: $23.601B actual versus $26.300B first post-Xilinx guidance, a **10.262% shortfall**, despite August reaffirmation. That is company history, not solely the current CFO's record. [Initial guidance](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1062/amd-reports-first-quarter-2022-financial-results), [year-end actual](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1115/amd-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2022-financial-results)

Conclusion: near-term delivery supports credible recent execution; long-range capital returns and the scale of AI deployment remain unproven. Q3's $13.0B ± $0.3B revenue and 56% non-GAAP margin guidance is **unscored**. Results are scheduled for November 3. [Q2 outlook](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1295/amd-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results), [reporting date](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1300/amd-to-report-fiscal-third-quarter-2026-financial-results)

The 2027 Data Center direction above 100% and server CPU direction above 70% are also unscored. Base/scale/delay 2027 Data Center assumptions stay at 90%/115%/45%. The latest Helion roadmap adds context, not separate forecast revenue; HUMAIN's reported live production is execution evidence, not proof of the entire planned buildout. [Q2 call](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_d22fb6007d12335ff19068b92f2958b1/amd/db/841/9237/webcast_transcript/AMD2Q26EarningsCallTranscript.pdf), [Helion](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1301/introducing-amd-helion-agentic-ai-compute-at-rack-scale), [HUMAIN](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1298/amd-cisco-and-humain-expand-saudi-arabias-ai-infrastructure-as-amd-instinct-systems-go-live)
